idiom_name: createOrder(raw): Order with a type guard
implementation_notes: The idiomatic TypeScript creation owner is a factory function whose return type is the domain type (or a discriminated union Order | ValidationError), with type guards or assertion functions narrowing unknown input before construction; because TypeScript erases types at runtime, the factory is also the only place where raw JSON stops being unknown. There is no constructor overloading and no way to hide a constructor, so named factory functions are simultaneously the naming mechanism and the validation seam; for untrusted data the schema-first variant is stronger, deriving the static type from the runtime schema so the two cannot drift.
pitfalls: Type assertions (as Order) and non-null ! are unchecked casts that defeat the factory; return a narrowed type or an explicit error union instead.
A factory returning a mutable object lets callers change it past its invariants; Readonly<T>, as const or class private fields keep it honest.
Declaring the interface separately from the validation logic invites drift; derive the type from the schema where a schema exists.

variants.name: Schema-first factory (zod safeParse)
variants.implementation_notes: Make one schema the single source of truth: define the shape and its rules with zod, derive the static type with z.infer, and expose a factory that calls safeParse and returns either the parsed value or a structured error. The runtime validator and the compile-time type come from the same artifact, which removes the drift that makes hand-written guards unsafe as they age; parse, do not validate.
pitfalls: parse() throws a ZodError while safeParse() returns a discriminated union; pick one at the boundary and do not let both leak into the domain.
By default unknown keys are stripped silently; use .strict() at boundaries where payload drift must surface.
A .transform() changes the output type, so z.infer is the post-transform type while z.input is the raw one - confusing them produces type errors or double coercion.
